## Active

### D-947 — The viewer realm answers viewer.* and needs no ingress

> _2026-11-21 · realm/blong-viewer · active_

The realm answers its own name: `viewer.entry.find` and `viewer.entry.search`, granted by one
capability `viewerRead`. The todos first wrote `log.entry.find` and a `log.viewer.open` capability;
that was withdrawn because `log` is already the framework's configuration namespace
(`log.destination`, `log.calls`, `log.capture`) and a realm's methods are named after the realm, so
a `log.*` route would have read as framework configuration and collided with it in a suite block.

No ingress and no proxy, which is the other half of D-946. The page is served by the process whose
gateway answers it, so the reader's calls go to the origin it was loaded from, carry the cookie and
the bearer token it already has, and are authorised by the same `access.authorization.list` step as
every other page. In a monolith profile — what every suite that publishes a portal does today — that
one process carries the realm, so nothing has to be routed. `k8sRealmRole: 'service'` says the realm
can own a process when a profile splits it out; a split deployment is then the one case that would
need the API reachable under a path on the portal's host, which the gateway does not serve yet and
no current suite asks for.

The buffer is memory and the realm has no database: the records a process wrote are what the buffer
holds since this process started, and a restart begins empty. The capability seed is the one `meta/`
file the realm keeps, and it is applied into blong-access's own tables by the deployment's
migration, not into a table of ours.

### D-953 — The viewer's UDP port is derived per package, 9999 where a dev rc exists

> _2026-11-21 · realm/blong-viewer · active_

The viewer's UDP port cannot be one constant and cannot be the kernel's choice. Three suites load
the realm, CI runs their packages side by side, and each bound 9999 until all but the first died
with EADDRINUSE. A kernel-chosen port does not fit either: the realm installs the writer that sends
as well as the receiver that listens, and the writer needs the number while the realm is starting.
So the port is derived the way the Playwright runner derives its gateway pair: 9600 plus the
package's index in rush.json, read by both halves from the realm, so they agree by construction and
two packages never share a number. The same decision moves the destination into the realm: a process
that was not told where its records go gets the receiver beside it, published by the loader as
manifest.logDestination from installDestination, which is why a suite that loads the viewer names
the realm alone and says nothing about an address. A configured destination always wins — in a
deployment every process names the Service, and the realm's release activation says so. Two runs
keep the conventional 9999: a machine with a developer's .blong_devrc, which writes the destination
once for every package it runs, and a tree with no rush.json, which is a container where 9999 is
what the Service targets. The gate on the rc is what keeps a local CI=1 run working, since the
listener would otherwise move to a derived port the developer's own destination never sends to.
